title: MCA Annual Filing FY 2025-26: No Extension Granted — ADT-1, AOC-4, MGT-7 Deadlines Stand
summary: ICSI asked MCA to extend annual filing deadlines to 31 December 2026, but no extension circular has been issued. ADT-1 was due 14 Oct, AOC-4 due 29 Oct, MGT-7 due 29 Nov — with Rs 100/day late fees running.
content:
Bottom line as on 24 October 2026: MCA has not extended the annual filing deadlines for FY 2025-26. ICSI's request of 9 October 2026 is still just a request — no General Circular has been issued. The statutory due dates stand, and additional fees of Rs 100 per day per form apply from day one of delay.

Quick Answer

On 9 October 2026, the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) wrote to the MCA Secretary asking that annual e-forms — AOC-4 and its variants, MGT-7/MGT-7A, plus DIR-12 and ADT-1 — be allowed to be filed up to 31 December 2026 without additional fees. As verified on MCA's official circulars listing on 24 October 2026, no such extension has been granted. The latest General Circular on mca.gov.in remains No. 04/2026 dated 31 August 2026 (about a different scheme, now closed). Until MCA issues a numbered General Circular, the Companies Act deadlines apply in full.

What ICSI Asked For

ICSI's representation (ref. G&CL: MCA: OCT:01/2026, dated 9 October 2026, addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs) seeks a one-time relaxation for the following forms, up to 31 December 2026, without levy of additional fees:

FormWhat it is
AOC-4 (and CFS / XBRL / NBFC-Ind AS / CFS NBFC-Ind AS variants)Filing of financial statements
MGT-7 / MGT-7AAnnual return (MGT-7A for smaller companies and OPCs)
ADT-1Intimation of auditor appointment
DIR-12Intimation of director appointment / resignation / change in designation

Why ICSI Asked

  • MCA-21 V3 portal trouble — downtime, slow responses, session timeouts, login problems, incorrect pre-filled data, DSC association failures, validation errors and payment/SRN difficulties.
  • Heavier forms — the revised AOC-4 and MGT-7 demand far more granular data and disclosures; XBRL tagging and reconciliation add preparation time.
  • Precedent — CBDT Circular No. 07/2026 dated 28 September 2026 extended the tax audit report deadline to 21 October 2026 and ITR for audit cases (AY 2026-27) to 21 November 2026.

What MCA Has Actually Done — Verified 24 Oct 2026

MCA's official General Circulars listing was checked on 15 October 2026 and re-checked on 24 October 2026. The position is unchanged: the latest General Circular is still No. 04/2026 dated 31-08-2026, and no circular extending FY 2025-26 annual filing deadlines has been issued.

Don't confuse the two. The CCFS-2026 scheme dealt with backlog filings and closed on 15 September 2026. It is not an extension of the current annual filing due dates.

Will MCA Extend the Deadline? Our Analysis

Analysis — the CorpLawUpdates view, not an MCA announcement. Everything above this section is verified fact. What follows is our reading of the signals, published because "will there be an extension?" is the question every filer is asking this week.

The case that relief comes

  • The failure is MCA's own portal. ICSI's representation of 9 October 2026 documents MCA-21 V3 downtime, session timeouts, login failures, DSC association errors, wrong pre-filled data and payment failures. When the regulator's own system is the bottleneck, relief has historically followed.
  • Last year, MCA did exactly this. For the FY 2024-25 annual filing season, MCA issued General Circular No. 06/2025 dated 17 October 2025 allowing annual filings without additional fees up to 31 December 2025 — and then General Circular No. 08/2025 dated 30 December 2025 extending the relaxation into January 2026.
  • CBDT has already moved. Circular No. 07/2026 dated 28 September 2026 extended the tax audit report date to 21 October 2026 and ITR filing for audit cases to 21 November 2026. ICSI's letter expressly asks MCA to match that approach.

The case for caution

  • MCA's current posture is enforcement, not relaxation. The Companies Compliance Facilitation Scheme, 2026 closed on 15 September 2026, and MCA has said Registrars will act against companies still in default.
  • The calendar is already later than last year. Last year's first relief circular came on 17 October. This year, 22 October has passed with nothing — and when relief came last year, the second circular arrived only on 30 December, after the deadlines had technically run out. MCA decides late, and sometimes not at all.
  • Relief may be narrower than the demand. ICSI has asked for filing up to 31 December 2026 without additional fees. What MCA grants — if anything — could be only a fee waiver for a shorter window, not a full extension.

Our verdict

A fee waiver is a realistic possibility — it is MCA's own pattern when its portal is the problem. But it cannot be planned on, and the cost of guessing wrong is one-sided: filing AOC-4 by 29 October 2026 costs nothing extra, while waiting costs Rs 100 per day, per form, with no cap if no circular comes. File on the statutory dates. If relief is announced, this page will be updated the same day.

Your Deadlines Haven't Moved

For the common case of an AGM held on 30 September 2026:

FormStatutory basisDue dateStatus
ADT-1Section 139(1) — within 15 days of AGM14 October 2026Due date passed — file now, Rs 100/day is running
AOC-4Section 137(1) — within 30 days of AGM29 October 20265 days left (as of 24 Oct 2026)
MGT-7 / MGT-7ASection 92(4) — within 60 days of AGM29 November 202636 days left (as of 24 Oct 2026)
Why 29 October and not 30? Sections 137 and 139 say "within thirty / fifteen days of the date of the AGM" — the AGM day itself counts, and MCA's own AOC-4 form help gives 29 October 2026 for a 30 September 2026 AGM. Section 92(4) for MGT-7 is worded "from the day of the AGM", which is why MGT-7 runs to 29 November. File by the earlier date — it costs nothing and removes the argument.

What Waiting Costs

Additional fees under Rule 12 of the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014 run at Rs 100 per day, per form — with no upper cap for delays beyond Sections 92(4) and 137(1). A 30-day delay on two forms is Rs 6,000; the meter keeps running indefinitely. Only a numbered MCA General Circular can waive these fees — a representation cannot.

What To Do Now

  • ADT-1 fell due on 14 October 2026 for a 30 September AGM — if it is still pending, file it today; the Rs 100/day meter is already running.
  • Treat 29 October (AOC-4) and 29 November (MGT-7) as hard dates until MCA says otherwise in a numbered circular.
  • Don't bank on the extension. Early filers lose nothing if it comes; late filers pay Rs 100/day/form if it doesn't.

MCA Site Not Working? How to Get Your Filing Through

Portal failure is the most common reason filings are stuck this season. These are the practical steps professionals are using — none of them changes your legal due date, so work through them early, not on the last day.

ProblemWhat to do
Portal slow or timing outFile off-peak — before 9 AM or after 8 PM IST — and avoid the final 48 hours before a due date, when traffic peaks. Complete one form per session; do not keep several MCA tabs open.
DSC association failsRe-associate the DSC in MCA-21 V3, make sure the name and PAN on the DSC match the MCA profile exactly, update the DSC utility software and restart the DSC service before retrying.
Payment debited, challan not generatedCheck the SRN's payment status before paying again — never pay twice for the same SRN. A generated challan remains valid for its stated period.
Wrong pre-filled dataRaise a ticket on MCA's helpdesk with screenshots and keep the ticket number. Wrong pre-fills are one of the specific failures ICSI's representation lists.
Any error that stops you filingKeep evidence: a screenshot of the error showing the date and time, plus the SRN you attempted. If MCA later waives fees for portal failure, that contemporaneous record is what proves you tried to file on time.

Important: a broken portal does not stop the clock. The Rs 100-per-day additional fee keeps running unless MCA issues a General Circular granting relief — which, as of 24 October 2026, it has not.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has MCA extended the AOC-4 / MGT-7 due dates for FY 2025-26?

No. As verified on MCA's official circulars listing on 24 October 2026, no General Circular extending FY 2025-26 annual filing deadlines has been issued.

Does ICSI's letter itself extend the deadline?

No. A representation is a request, not a legal instrument. Only a numbered MCA General Circular can extend a statutory deadline or waive additional fees.

What is the late filing fee?

Rs 100 per day per form under the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014, with no maximum cap.

The MCA website is not working. Will the due date be extended automatically?

No. Portal difficulty does not change a statutory due date, and the Rs 100-per-day additional fee keeps running unless MCA issues a General Circular granting relief. Portal failures are the main ground in ICSI's representation of 9 October 2026, but as verified on 24 October 2026, MCA has not announced any decision. Keep screenshots and SRN details as evidence, and file as soon as the portal allows.

Source Note

MCA position verified: General Circulars listing on mca.gov.in, checked 15 October 2026 and re-checked 24 October 2026 — latest General Circular No. 04/2026 dated 31-08-2026; no FY 2025-26 annual filing extension exists.
ICSI representation: G&CL: MCA: OCT:01/2026 dated 9 October 2026 (as reported in professional press).
Statutory basis: Sections 92(4), 137(1), 139(1), Companies Act, 2013; Rule 12, Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014.

For information only; not legal advice. Verify dates against your company's AGM.
